content.intro: Learn configuring project settings through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Configuring Project Settings matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines configuring project settings as part of django project structure and configuration. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: DEBUG; SECRET_KEY; ALLOWED_HOSTS; ROOT_URLCONF; DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD; Reading settings and using environment-specific values. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: DEBUG
items.text: Treat DEBUG as a reproducible diagnostic: capture the exact input and observed result, isolate one hypothesis, and add a regression test once the cause is fixed. Avoid exposing internal stack traces or secrets to public users.

items.title: SECRET_KEY
items.text: SECRET_KEY is a server-side responsibility where applicable. Define who may perform the action and on which object, validate untrusted input, test denied cases, and document sensitive-data handling.

items.title: ALLOWED_HOSTS
items.text: For ALLOWED_HOSTS, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: ROOT_URLCONF
items.text: ROOT_URLCONF is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD
items.text: DEFAULT_AUTO_FIELD affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

items.title: Reading settings and using environment-specific values
items.text: Configuration for Reading settings and using environment-specific values should be explicit, environment-aware, and validated before serving requests. Record defaults and deploy-specific values, keep secrets outside committed content, and test the setting that changes behavior.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Configuring Project Settings
content_blocks.code:
import os

DEBUG = os.environ.get("DJANGO_DEBUG", "false").lower() == "true"
SECRET_KEY = os.environ["DJANGO_SECRET_KEY"]
ALLOWED_HOSTS = os.environ.get("DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS", "localhost").split(",")
content_blocks.expected_output: Settings are read from environment variables. Missing required secrets fail early instead of silently shipping a hardcoded value.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Open a local project using the documented Django 6.1-compatible Python environment. If this snippet depends on model names, URL configuration, settings, or an optional package, add those prerequisites before running it. Otherwise inspect it as a static example. CodeLeaf browser preview does not execute Django/Python server code.
content_blocks.troubleshooting: For production use a secret manager/environment configuration, DEBUG=False, a reviewed ALLOWED_HOSTS list, HTTPS, and django check --deploy. Do not commit real secret values.

content_blocks.text: Change one input or configuration choice related to DEBUG. Write down the expected outcome, test one normal case and one invalid or boundary case, then record what changed. Do not add real credentials or sensitive production data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
